why: One light board: a browser card on the left with a form and a Submit button, a server card on the right, a slate router box between them with a watcher marker. On Submit, a packet carrying readable text leaves the browser along the path.
The packet passes the watcher box, which duplicates it; the copy shows the same readable form fields, held beside the original so both read identically.
The same board holds still; a small open padlock icon appears above the path and the watcher's copy blurs slightly as a promise of the outcome, without changing the layout.
A request arrow runs from browser to server; a certificate card slides back to the browser showing a site name and a small authority seal that appears on the last phrase.
On the certificate card at the browser, three teal ticks appear one at a time beside name, expiry and issuer fields, each on its phrase.
The certificate card shrinks to a ticked badge; an empty key slot appears at each end of the path, with the watcher still between them.
Two small value tokens cross the path in opposite directions; the watcher copies each into a tray, and a blank key slot stays empty beside the watcher.
Matching blue keys appear in the slots at browser and server only; the watcher's slot remains empty.
The ticked badge enlarges beside the keys and its three ticks re-light in turn, tying the key to the passed check.
The form data block at the browser, readable, passes through the blue key and turns into scrambled blocks as it leaves.
Scrambled blocks travel past the watcher, whose copy is the same unreadable pattern; a small label shows the server address still visible, content not.
At the server the scrambled blocks pass the key and turn readable again; a reply packet then travels back as scrambled blocks and turns readable at the browser.
The same request goes to a new server whose certificate card shows a different name; three option cards appear side by side on their phrases, none marked.
The name tick on the certificate card turns red and the warning option card lights; the continue-quietly card dims with a note that scrambling alone leaves the far end unknown.
An address bar appears with a generic padlock; two teal labels attach to the padlock on the two phrases.
Two slate 'does not show' labels are added beside the padlock; the server card at the end of the path shows the form data readable again.
Two ticks are added in the address bar: the site name is highlighted letter by letter, then a warning banner slot is shown empty.
The opening board returns unchanged: form, path, watcher. The packet crosses as scrambled blocks, the watcher's copy is noise, and the padlock above the path closes.

choice: Router L-431: a defect on an element b01 drew that happens in a later holding beat goes to that beat. Run 2d with --budget 5.

why: Element band_dark overlays the whole frame (opacity 0.45 ink) at t=48.5s, darkening the white browser card and reducing User and Password text contrast to 2.19:1 (fails 3:1 minimum).

data.fix: In scenes/b07.js, place band_dark behind the held board or dim the canvas background token instead of drawing a full-frame 45% ink overlay on top of the cards, keeping cards light and type contrast above 4.5:1.

why: The watcher tray still displays the Value tokens from b07, and the scrambled copy block is drawn directly on top of them at x=860 y=610, covering 86% of the Value text and causing a contrast failure (1.34:1).

data.fix: In scenes/b11.js, set board.handle.setState('tray_empty', ctx.start) on the held board before revealing the scrambled copy element, so the previous Value tokens are cleared.

why: The label server_tag at x=1110 y=596 with width 345 overlaps the server card, covering 28% of accounts.example text, and runs off the right frame edge in camera zoom.

data.fix: In scenes/b11.js, move server_tag to x=860 y=710 or decrease its width so it sits entirely below the watcher tray and leaves the server card untouched.

why: The camera push in b09 leaves the browser key slot 84% outside the right edge of the frame, cutting off the object meant to be associated with the checklist.

data.fix: In scenes/b09.js or storyboard.json b09 shot.focus, widen the camera view to x=100 y=140 w=800 h=600 so the browser key slot remains fully inside safe margins.

why: In the wide view, the watcher tray still displays messy visual residue of the Value tokens sticking out beneath the scrambled blocks.

data.fix: In scenes/b12.js, verify board.handle tray state is set to tray_noise or tray_empty without residual Value tokens beneath the scrambled blocks.

why: All three quiz options from b13 are re-rendered floating above the router in b14 arrive, creating visual clutter and exceeding the element density budget (9 chunks).

data.fix: In scenes/b14.js, omit flag_quiet and flag_plain so only the active Warn you flag appears, keeping chunk density within the 5 to 6 budget.

why: In b11 join (73.55s) and arrive (74.25s), scrambled packet blocks are rendered directly over the router box and eye graphic before the move begins, creating double-exposure residue across the central watcher device.

data.fix: In scenes/b11.js, exit the held packet at ctx.start and create a fresh packet element at the b10 settled position (x=720, y=420) to travel past the watcher, preventing the engine's second m.travel drive from rendering premature residue at load over the router box and eye.
